speaker_notes: The V2 circuit combines the input filter and rectifier, charge-pump and resonant branches, GaN half bridge, transformer, and secondary rectifier. The drawing shows the circuit before the tank change, with the external series inductor L4 still present. The charge-pump conversion principle and analytical design method came from earlier work by Ahmed M. Ammar, Frederik M. Spliid, Yasser Nour, and Arnold Knott. Their papers are “Analysis and Design of a Charge-Pump-Based Resonant AC–DC Converter With Inherent PFC Capability,” IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Power Electronics, 2020, DOI 10.1109/JESTPE.2020.2966143, and “A 1-MHz Resonant LED Driver With Charge-Pump-Based Power Factor Correction,” the same journal, 2021, DOI 10.1109/JESTPE.2021.3083404. The planar inductor and transformer came from earlier DTU work by Bima Nugraha Sanusi and the DTU Power Electronics group; component measurements were made by Máni Gautason. This project integrated the supplied magnetics and developed the hardware, control, sensing, local supplies and USB-C interface, then tested the assembled supply.
